General complex square/reciprocal tolerance is relative6e-7 for complex64 and2e-15 for wider complex types; thirty-eight FMA layout/writeback cases compare exactly; all observed new numerical errors were zero
Coercion uses the existing constructor; ordinary string-to-numeric table construction and all nested typed-array combinations remain incomplete

Fmod compares exactly in new fixtures; float_power and existing power/arctan2/hypot use relative2e-12 tolerance; observed float_power relative error3.2300436499022e-15 and absolute3.1974423109205e-14
String add supports fixed-width S+S and U+U, canonical endian and staged output casts; variable StringDType and mixed S/U are unsupported
Lua raw strings default to Unicode unless paired with an explicit S/U array; separate Python bytes/str scalar classes are not reproduced
Binary logical promotion follows boolean conversion before computation, including tiny weak float/complex scalars and fixed-width strings; unary logical_not has separate supported signatures
Layout values, metadata, sharing, actual writable status and post-write backing states compare exactly in 25134 new cases; empty allocations and reshape views can have distinct strides
Reshape accepts one Lua integer/table shape plus C/F/A and copy=true/false/if_needed; full historical NumPy variadic shape signatures, device/subclass/foreign protocols remain incomplete
Ravel/flatten K-order preserves negative logical traversal and stable zero-stride ambiguity; all host ABI/foreign malformed array layouts are not certified
Reshape copy=false applies after ordinary Lua inputs are coerced to a temporary array; this differs from asarray copy=false, which forbids its own necessary allocation
Component real/imag views preserve typed storage and identity; direct ndarray.real/imag property replacement setters remain unsupported; write through the returned view instead
Root real/imag ordinary scalar results follow the typed rank-zero ndarray convention; full Python scalar/subclass/device protocols remain incomplete
Reality predicates distinguish values from dtype; value results are typed bool arrays while object predicates return Lua booleans
Real_if_close supports weak Lua numeric/integer/boolean tolerances; nil means default100; ndarray-valued tolerances and complete Python argument protocols remain unsupported
Real_if_close casts tolerance at component precision, scales tol>1 by epsilon and compares strictly; exact x87 boundary references are built via real native ldexp/stack/component writes
Legacy Lua astype string conversions follow ndarray.astype rather than NumPy root Array API numeric-only signature; complex strings round through two doubles even for clongdouble

Complex text parsing now accepts valid overflow/underflow and rejects malformed underscores, C hexadecimal/nan-payload syntax and embedded NUL in nonboolean numeric strings; full Unicode decimal/space grammar and locale-independent parsing remain pending
Round preserves typed composition, complex component assignment and root TypeError retry; Lua errors remain ordinary Lua errors rather than Python exception objects
Internal ln_error gained a category field; development-version C consumers must rebuild all native objects; full error-class coverage is not certified
Power-of-ten uses source multiplication order through308 and stabilized infinity from309; INT_MIN/MAX native bounds tested without executing upstream billion-step loops

Floating timedelta multiply/divide uses the source double loop including longdouble coefficients and x86 NaT overflow results; integer division, timedelta ratios and complete temporal arithmetic remain unimplemented
Round Lua options/typed scalar return adaptation and constructor limits remain; every subclass/device/foreign protocol, FP status/rounding mode and host ABI is not certified
Clip supports positional bounds and out/where options; Python keyword aliases and dtype/casting/order/signature/subok are not accepted
Clip resolves strong descriptor categories before weak value packing, implements integer-bound elision and fused numeric/time loops; complete foreign DType and scalar protocols remain unavailable

Uniform non-reduction buffer cost planning is currently selected for clip, using the source default8192; Python setbufsize, every possible memory layout, warnings, NaN payloads and host floating environment remain uncertified
View reinterprets supported descriptor bytes and shares the owner; changing itemsize follows last-axis contiguity/divisibility, with scalar/singleton/empty rules and overflow checks
Tobytes exports actual bytes including padding; NumPy2.5.3 K uses C order for numeric/bytes/time but KEEPORDER ravel for Unicode; letters case-insensitive, Lua nil/default C
View accepts dtype strings only; Python subclasses/type arguments, void/subarray/structured/object/variableStringDType and non-native numeric endian remain unsupported

Alignment flags and scalar loads/stores plus generic/legacy iterators and core reduction/accumulation staging support directed unaligned cases; every downstream algorithm and foreign storage layout is not certified
Frozen raw-byte oracles use little-endian x86-64; independently constructed longdouble padding and all foreign ABIs are not certified

Cross follows NumPy2.5.3 three-component inputs, common-dtype casts and output-last allocation plus axis view; positive Lua axes are one-based and root ordinary array-like inputs use the existing constructor

General complex cross budgets are fixed at6e-7 for complex64 and2e-15 for wider complex, scaled by max(1,abs(component)); exact state/metadata/zero/nonfinite cases are separate; byte-identical CPU FMA dispatch is not certified

Meshgrid uses an explicit Lua input sequence table and returns a sequence table; copy/sparse require Lua booleans; indexing is xy/ij; Python variadic/custom protocols and warning objects are not reproduced

Meshgrid copy=false preserves source writable/readonly broadcasting and may share inputs or other cells; incompatible input flattening can still copy; inferred reshape preserves empty/singleton strides
Root diagonal uses the first two axes by default; linalg.diagonal uses the last two; extracted views are read-only
Diagonal extraction uses the native C int offset range; construction uses checked native-size dimensions; foreign index objects and complete Python signature/dispatch fidelity are not implemented

Diagonal index helpers return a Lua sequence of shared one-based index vectors; diag_indices_from requires an actual ndarray with equal-sized axes. Python index/tuple/subclass protocols are not reproduced.

Triangular index helpers return two independent contiguous one-based index vectors; _from requires a two-dimensional ndarray and accepts rectangular matrices. Strict Lua integer and Lua sequence conventions replace Python protocols.

Fill_diagonal uses logical C iteration with live same-dtype aliases, cycling values and Boolean wrap. Lua options and scalar bounds differ from typed unsafe casting; full foreign scalar, subclass and warning protocols are not reproduced.
Kron coerces both inputs to strong arrays, interleaves axes and uses C-order reshape. Scalar-right and scalar-left rank limits differ as in NumPy2.5.3; scalar results are typed rank-zero ndarrays.
General kron random complex64 values use relative3e-7 and wider float/complex relative3e-15; exact ordinary values, signed zeros and metadata are separate. Observed new numerical errors were zero.

Integer duration multiplication uses int64 coefficient conversion, NaT propagation and checked overflow. Completed writes, mask-run continuation and tested buffer/negative-stride traversal match references; every possible foreign/output/iterator layout is not certified.

In176 failed buffered unit-conversion cases, upstream flushes nondeterministic uninitialized suffix cells. Only defined prefix values and full metadata are compared; LuaRay preserves unwritten cells. Full suffix/exception-message parity is not claimed.
Tensordot adapts positive axes to one-based Lua integers and returns typed rank-zero arrays. Negative count means no contraction. Python iterable/subclass protocols remain unsupported.

Tensordot has154 executed object-result cases explicitly blocked, excluded from parity-eligible counts. BLAS result zero signs are not certified across vendors:44 observed sign differences; input zero signs and non-BLAS result zeros remain exact.
General random contraction tolerances are absolute+relative3e-6 for float32/complex64 and2e-12 for wider float/complex types; exact ordinary nonzero values and metadata are separate.
Legacy timedelta dot uses raw int64 wrapping after common-unit conversion and treats NaT as raw bits, matching arraytypes.c.src rather than ordinary duration multiplication.

Mask_indices is a Lua composition over native kernels. It accepts ordinary sequence callback results through asarray and ignores extra callback returns. Numeric one-based coordinates and Lua nil/callable conventions are explicit adaptations.

Mask_indices preserves the source ndarray rich-comparison behavior for strings and datetime rather than incorrectly substituting their boolean cast. Callback scalar results remain invalid; full object and foreign dispatch protocols are unavailable.

Diff and ediff1d use Lua options and strict one-based axes. Diff n=0 returns the original Lua input without coercion; native-max order is locally executed using stable-empty termination, not run through the enormous upstream loop.

Ediff1d uses an options table for padding and retains the source dtype with same_kind validation; Boolean and padded datetime subtraction follow pinned rejection rules. Complete Python argument/subclass/foreign protocols remain unsupported.

Native concatenate/stack selects strides with the source multi-input ordering and empty-allocation rules. The trivial ufunc allocation path now accepts equally shaped contiguous multiple inputs, preserving canonical C/F singleton strides.
Gradient uses a Lua options table with one-based axes and per-axis spacings. Python variadic arguments, foreign/subclass protocols and complete warning/scalar classes remain unsupported.
Gradient floating result budgets are absolute+relative5e-3 for half,5e-6 for float32/complex64 and2e-12 for wider types. Observed new numerical errors were zero.

Integer duration true division truncates toward zero with int64 divisors, NaT/zero handling and checked output-unit conversions. Duration ratios cast to a common unit then compute float64; incompatible calendar/fixed units reject. Complete temporal arithmetic remains partial.

Trapezoid uses a Lua options table and typed rank-zero results. Computation order preserves integer wrap and temporal tick truncation. Full foreign/subclass/scalar/warning protocols are not reproduced.
Trapezoid general numeric budgets are absolute+relative5e-3 half,5e-6 float32/complex64,2e-12 wider. Observed new max absolute8.8817841970013e-16 and relative2.6737044432591e-16.

Unwrap uses a Lua options table and strict integer axes. Integer periods preserve source half-interval parity and native modular differences; scalar boundary truth errors and floating broadcasting are tested. Complete foreign/subclass/scalar/warning protocols remain unsupported.

Angle composes real/imaginary views with native arctan2 and optional in-place degree scaling. Lua deg requires a Boolean; scalar results are typed rank-zero arrays. Full foreign/subclass/scalar/warning protocols remain unsupported.
Angle relative budgets are half2e-3,float32 3e-6,wider2e-12. Observed max absolute1.52587890625e-05 and relative1.4020190897517e-07; exact signed zeros are separate.

Interp uses a Lua options table and typed rank-zero scalar results. Query/sample conversion differs with and without period as in the source. Scalar periods are restricted to real Lua numbers or real rank-zero arrays.

Interpolation sorting follows the existing portable NumPy-derived quicksort.68 new ambiguous periodic cases use the NumPy kernel after generic portable quicksort;12 differ from the default CPU-optimized wheel. CPU-specific unstable tie ordering is not certified.

Interp numeric references allow absolute+relative2e-12, with zero observed error against the declared reference. Object/structured/foreign protocols, complete warning/scalar classes and all CPU implementations remain unsupported.

Equality/closeness use Lua options tables and Boolean equal_nan. Array_equal and array_equiv return Lua Booleans; isclose scalar results remain typed rank-zero arrays. Full foreign/subclass/Python scalar/warning/error-state protocols are not reproduced.

Array rich equality handles known absent dtype-family signatures separately from execution or metadata errors; incompatible calendar/fixed duration comparison still raises. Signed-integer no-NaN fast paths exclude timedelta despite its integer-subtype classification.

Temporal add/subtract and predicates use the native iterator. Integer offsets preserve units; unsigned64 arithmetic is allowed but duration/unsigned64 comparison remains unsupported as in the pinned source. Failed arithmetic preserves completed prefix/mask-run writes.
New extended-precision reference inputs normalize x87 padding and retain all value bits. Other host floating ABIs and all nondefault rounding/error-state modes remain uncertified.

Ndarray item uses strict one-based Lua integer indices and one coordinate table. Longdouble/complex256 and high uint64 values return detached typed rank-zero arrays; temporal elements retain LuaRay temporal userdata instead of Python datetime/timedelta/None conversion.

Fill packs before writes including empty arrays, captures aliased values, uses Boolean sequence truth and preserves scalar versus rank-zero casting distinctions. Full object/structured/foreign/Python scalar and warning/error protocols remain unsupported.

Datetime year/month casts use actual calendar conversion; pinned source integer wrap in calendar formulas and scalar item-range decisions is implemented without signed overflow UB. Duration casts retain average units and temporal text casts retain the observed21-character legacy limit.

Temporal transfer availability is resolved before data iteration, including empty arrays. Literal false copyto masks preserve the distinct scalar-preconversion and array-assignment shortcuts; regression checks retain the previous scalar string conversion rules.

frombuffer accepts binary Lua strings and C-contiguous native ndarrays; arbitrary foreign buffer, like and subclass protocols are unavailable. Count and offset must be strict Lua integers; byte offsets start at zero. Non-native numeric endian descriptors remain unsupported.

Lua strings are pinned and read-only through all views. C external buffers transfer their optional callback/context only on successful construction; null callbacks leave lifetime with the caller. Lua-owned buffers must not outlive their Lua state.

Expanded instrumentation found and fixed an earlier scalar-assignment stack buffer that was too small for complex256; the final audit includes ln_core and the dedicated regression. Other dependencies remain only partially instrumented.

setflags supports write/align as optional strict Boolean positional values or Lua options. WRITEBACKIFCOPY/uic mutation and its Python base-detachment/writeback protocol remain unsupported; the engine never exposes that flag as active.

Flags objects retain source snapshot semantics and retain their referenced array; attributes and string mapping keys share one Lua namespace. Python flag-object warning/subclass/truth-conversion protocols and exact text representation are not reproduced.

Logical root write permission is stored with the storage owner for surviving views. Native integrations must use ln_array_setflags for logical permission changes rather than directly clearing an owning root flag. Physical readonly storage cannot be unlocked.

require accepts nil/false/empty requirements, character strings or dense Lua string sequences; arbitrary Python dictionaries/iterators, like and subclass protocols are unsupported. E is satisfied by the sole native Lua array class.

Dtype-changing ANYORDER creation transfers preserve KEEPORDER axis layout, while same-dtype ANYORDER copy shortcuts remain distinct. This targeted correction does not certify every array creation/cast/foreign-dispatch case.

shape/ndim/size read native ndarray metadata directly; other supported Lua values use existing native creation/discovery, so nested ndarray/foreign/object/nil scalar and protocol limitations remain. Shapes are fresh Lua sequences, not Python tuples.
size accepts one strict Lua integer axis, positive from one or negative from the end; zero and unsupported axis protocols raise. No Python shape/ndim/size attribute dispatch is implemented.

dtype exposes immutable native scalar descriptors and the documented fields only. Python scalar classes/ctypes/foreign/structured/subarray/object/void/StringDType protocols, align/copy/metadata constructor options, type/isbuiltin/newbyteorder and other unlisted properties are unsupported. array.dtype and promotion results retain existing Lua strings.

Core dtype readers accept descriptors; some legacy readers including random-generator controls still require strings. Native character/width/endian forms are supported within the existing scalar-kind scope. Non-native numeric/temporal formats remain blocked. The old float->float32 alias was corrected to NumPy float64; use float32 or f for single precision.

Reduction dtype controls select general classes and reject width/endian/time details before empty shortcuts. Legacy ndarray cumulative adapters discard concrete metadata. Legacy timedelta/string addition selection quirks are preserved for verified cases.

Duration sum/mean/accumulate/reduceat preserve units, propagate selected NaT, use truncating integer means and checked addition including reserved-NaT overflow. Masks and initial values are tested; every out/alias/cross-unit/post-error output state is not certified.

Unsized string joins resolve from descriptors without inspecting contents; one same-class input retains its Unicode endian while common-instance combination normalizes. Sampling final casts resolve the source calculation formatting width.

ndarray constructor accepts documented dense integer shape/layout and scalar dtype descriptors; retained Lua string or C/F-contiguous ndarray buffers only. No Python arbitrary buffer/subclass/foreign-array protocols.

ndarray deliberately rejects unsafe or unverified upstream states: negative/excessive buffer offsets, inferred-stride footprints outside actual storage, zero-width inference, empty external buffers with nonempty payloads and overflowing element counts. The 2420 skipped reference parameter states are not compatibility passes. Native/Lua regressions directly test safety rejection.

Owned zero-byte ndarray allocations reset strides, while buffer views retain them. S0/U0 retain zero width here; existing empty constructors normalize widths. Constructor contiguity flags preserve upstream default-versus-explicit stride distinctions.

arange supports Lua numeric scalars, numeric rank-zero arrays, temporal scalars/arrays and temporal-converter strings/integers within documented scope. Higher-rank arguments, foreign numeric/like/device protocols and Python integers outside Lua range remain unsupported.

Legacy integer stop plus positional dtype preserves per-index conversion, including arbitrary-length Boolean ranges, raw temporal ticks and empty string descriptors. Options tables select the new NumPy constructor contract.

Lua-scalar arange computes source length and first two scalar conversions, then typed-delta filling with integer wrap. The new Boolean constructor has at most two elements. Lua complex scalar inputs require complex output; typed arithmetic follows its separate source scalar conversion rules.

The 0.142 scalar arange reference corpus excludes 138 oversized or outside-Lua-integer parameter cases. Longdouble padding bytes are omitted explicitly; significant bytes remain exact. Full host ABI, floating warning/error policy and all oversized allocations are not certified.

Typed arange uses native weak/array arithmetic and preserves original-array versus computed-scalar packing. Intermediate precision, integer wrap, default output promotion and complex128 versus complex64/complex256 length conversion follow the verified source cases. This does not certify every operand/value/ABI combination.

Original complex64/complex128 arrays reject ordinary real/integer scalar conversion; longdouble conversion has a separate source path. Numeric warning/error configuration and warning messages remain uncertified.

The 0.143 typed numeric reference corpus excludes 56 oversized allocations and 70 rejected source-array constructions before arange execution. These are not compatibility passes. Longdouble padding is canonicalized in fixture initializers and omitted from numerical comparisons.

Temporal arange performs same-kind conversion, metadata GCD resolution, calendar date conversion, normalized relative endpoints and integer tick filling. Generic output class is retained while units are inferred. Numeric array arguments to the temporal converter and Python datetime/foreign object protocols remain unsupported.

Explicit numeric output selects source numeric dispatch; temporal quotients retain their integer-item and division semantics. Original temporal scalars and rank-zero arrays keep distinct packing behavior through scalar_object provenance. ln_ufunc_operand layout changed: native consumers must rebuild against matching development headers.

Temporal metadata promotion casts to the common class before common-instance resolution, while ufunc input casts enforce default same_kind separately. Complete ufunc casting options/output aliasing/error-state fidelity remain uncertified.

Temporal relative endpoints normalize before NaT validation, preserving the tested upstream relative-NaT empty-range quirk. Zero steps and final NaT ticks are errors. Unit multipliers must be positive.

Relative-stop addition and temporal length numerators are checked before allocation; unsafe signed-int64 upstream overflow states and oversized allocations were excluded from oracle execution, not counted as passes. Native regressions directly test rejection.

Resize follows C-ravel/repeated-concatenate/prefix/reshape, including empty-like width normalization and default native Unicode descriptor resolution. Zero-width default reshape flags now preserve source stride-fill flags. Object/structured/StringDType and foreign protocols remain unsupported.

ndarray.resize uses one Lua shape argument and optional Boolean refcheck table. Lua aliases to the same userdata remain valid; byte-changing reallocations with native views are always rejected even with refcheck=false. Same-byte shape changes can retain shared buffers.

Read-only numeric growth leaves an unspecified tail as upstream; references never read it. Unicode growth is initialized even read-only deliberately. All negative dimensions and nonzero-axis stride products are validated after empty axes; unsafe source validation bypasses are not reproduced.

ndarray.byteswap supports a Boolean or inplace option table, source ANYORDER copies and in-place mutation with unchanged descriptors. Source complex component-pass and Unicode code-point traversal order is preserved for bounded overlapping layouts. Foreign protocols, object/structured and variable-width string dtypes remain unsupported.

Byte swapping reverses full extended component storage including padding, which the new references compare exactly. Swapped Unicode may be invalid until its representation or descriptor matches; no unsafe decoded values are used as oracle inputs.

Zero-width S/U exact/bounds queries now retain the source omitted-width/reflected-address solver convention. Existing exact-query work/memory caps remain; general unbounded Diophantine solving and all host ABIs are not certified. This query convention does not change zero-byte write semantics.

Per-item getfield/setfield preserve shape/strides and retain native storage with checked C-int byte offsets. Object/structured/StringDType and general foreign protocols remain unsupported; fields do not implement structured records.

Equal-shape ordinary Lua sequences pack progressively like CopyObject; later failures retain defined written prefixes. Broadcasting sequences use a temporary. Typed ndarrays use unsafe assignment and overlap handling. General nested typed arrays or temporal userdata in Lua sequences remain uncertified.

Temporal scalar field packing differs from ndarray casting: signed item conversion/bounds and scalar-date text follow their separate paths. Duration text retains the legacy cast limit of 21 characters. Full temporal scalar formatting is shared with existing duration casts, without changing public tostring.
Empty field offsets form integer addresses without out-of-allocation pointer arithmetic or dereference; zero-width field views retain original widths and the audited source memory-query convention.

ndarray conj/conjugate return the original real numeric userdata or execute native conjugation for complex input. Optional output uses same-kind real assignment or the complex ufunc path; foreign protocols, subclasses and all host ABIs remain uncertified.
The conjugation method accepts an output ndarray directly or an out options table. Other ufunc controls are not exposed by this method. String and temporal inputs are rejected.

Complex rank-zero method results without output follow LuaRay unary typed-array returns. Twenty-four reference scalars were normalized explicitly; their numerical bytes/dtypes are exact while ownership/writeability/post-write checks target the declared Lua representation.

indices accepts dense integer Lua dimension tables, descriptor/string dtype and strict Boolean sparse options; dense output adds an axis (63 dimension inputs), sparse permits 64. Source sparse negative-stop/reshape and unused-dtype rank-zero behavior are retained. Foreign shape objects/protocols remain unsupported.

ix_ retains numeric input values and typed-empty dtypes, converts ordinary empty sequences to intp and Boolean vectors to existing one-based nonzero locations. Reshape views preserve sharing and lifetime; downstream indexing still requires valid index dtypes/values.

argwhere uses logical nonzero locations in one-based coordinate rows, with source scalar shapes (1,0)/(0,0). Nil follows false-scalar truth; generic object/structured/StringDType arrays remain unavailable. Full nested coercions and all host ABIs are uncertified.

fromfunction creates dense grids and invokes a Lua callable once; all callback results are forwarded without coercion. Default coordinate dtype float64; only dtype is an options key. Dense grid rank limits and dtype restrictions apply before the callback.

Extra Lua parameters follow coordinates and preserve nil arity. Python keyword forwarding uses Lua positional/context-table conventions; foreign like/array protocols and all callback/host ABI interactions remain uncertified.

ndindex is a lazy Lua coordinate iterator with copied shape, independent snapshots and C order. Unlike ndarray, logical iterator rank is not capped at 64; source NumPy2.5.3 uses itertools.product. Huge logical dimensions do not materialize ranges or a total product counter.

Only Lua integer/Boolean dimensions or dense dimension tables are accepted. Python shape/__index__ protocols and integers beyond Lua range remain unsupported; Python iterator/StopIteration objects map to Lua closure/nil exhaustion.

Large cross-product references compare bounded prefixes. Huge individual source ranges were not allocated; native lazy behavior was tested separately, not claimed as identical resource-limit behavior.

apply_along_axis uses shared 1D views, C-order callback iteration and first-result buffer allocation/transpose. Lua axes are one-based and extra parameters preserve nil arity. Callback mutations and errors retain already written input state.

Only the first callback return is coerced to ndarray. Plain Lua scalar dtype inference replaces NumPy scalar-class protocols; Python keyword parameters use trailing Lua arguments. Object/structured dtypes, subclasses, foreign dispatch and all callback/casting/host ABI combinations remain uncertified.

apply_over_axes coerces Lua input/callback results to arrays, accepts an integer axis or dense integer Lua sequence, preserves ordered/repeated callbacks and restores one lost axis. Empty axes return the input. Scalar dtype inference is a declared Lua adaptation; ndarray axes, Boolean/float axis protocols, subclasses and foreign dispatch remain unsupported.
squeeze preserves userdata identity when no axes are removed. A nonempty reduction axis table is invalid for rank-zero input, while scalar Lua axes1/-1 retain the source special case.

Zero-width S0/U0 string sum follows non-reorderable addition with no identity, explicit mask/seed requirements, descriptor/out resolution and initialized zero-stride results. Ordinary nonzero-width string sum remains rejected. General string seeds and variable StringDType remain unavailable.

Numeric sum commits seeds before string conversion errors for disjoint non-scalar inputs/outputs. General overlapping string/numeric reduction failure writeback and output/mask overlap remain uncertified and retain staged execution.

The source oracle isolates dtype/output combinations in fresh NumPy processes after reproducing history-dependent dispatch. These cache-history variations are not a Lua compatibility target; scalar adapters and ABI padding exclusions are explicit.

Integer invert/count/shifts/gcd/lcm use native ArrayMethods with shared broadcasting, masks, alias protection and same-kind output. Only out/where table keys are accepted; full ufunc methods and dtype/casting/order protocols remain unavailable.

Population count uses absolute signed magnitude and returns uint8. Default shifts distinguish exact array signatures from weak scalar/default-loop alias selection; uniform gcd/lcm promote aliases separately and reject an all-Boolean dtype. All host ABIs and operand combinations remain uncertified.

Lua array ~, << and >> follow the NumPy integer operation semantics. Negative counts do not reverse direction; signed right shifts extend the sign, oversized shifts give zero/sign fill, and weak scalar bounds are checked before execution.

Boolean-to-numeric casts normalize truth for noncanonical raw bytes; same-descriptor Boolean identity copies preserve bytes. Numeric promotion now mirrors the source upper triangle to keep equivalent alias choices symmetric.

The sanitizer driver now derives object rebuilds from its declared unit/harness lists and verifies ASan initialization symbols in every listed object. The initial 0.153 audit overcounted instrumented native harnesses by one; a corrected repeat audit of its unchanged commit passed and was published separately.

Ravel/unravel use one-based integer locations. Zero is invalid when visited; ravel raise rejects negative values, wrap uses modulo and clip clamps negatives. Literal Boolean true is Lua location one and false is invalid zero, a declared language difference.

Ravel supports up to 63 coordinate axes, 64 broadcast dimensions and whole coordinate ndarrays including scalar-vector containers. Unravel supports target rank 64 and index rank 63; returned arrays are rooted writable views of new interleaved storage, not independent coordinate allocations.

Strict nonnegative Lua integer/table shapes and C/F order replace Python shape/sequence protocols. Ordinary inferred empty index tables, float/complex/string/time indices, unknown options and malformed mode names are rejected. Full foreign inputs, non-native numeric endian, every host ABI/resource limit and every input combination remain uncertified.

The shared KEEPORDER helper preserves the existing iterator sort and handles minimum signed strides without signed absolute-value overflow; the generic ufunc operand cap remains unchanged. Six existing take/indexing multiplication guards now honor the overflow helper Boolean failure contract.

Bincount counts zero-origin nonnegative integer/Boolean category data. All integer labels forcecast to native intp, including wide-unsigned wrap; negative converted labels and maximum-intp output-size overflow are rejected. Output is owned native intp or weighted float64.

Weighted bincount accumulates sequentially in logical input order using safe typed conversion to float64. Empty labels still validate rank/dtype/minlength but ignore weights and return intp zeros. Read-only/unaligned/stepped/broadcast inputs remain unchanged.

Bincount exposes strict weights/minlength Lua options or positional arguments; typed scalar minlength, foreign/index protocols, numeric strings in ordinary weight sequences, Python warning/exception classes, enormous source allocations, every ABI and every input combination remain uncertified.

Packbits accepts integer/Boolean data, treats all nonzero bytes as true, and zero-pads its final byte. Unpackbits requires uint8 and supports count truncation, zero extension or negative tail trimming. Empty-axis padding returns before calculating input addresses, including extreme-stride views. Both return owned writable uint8 data, use C flattening by default and preserve source C/F output allocation rules for explicit axes.

The pinned source explicit-axis legacy iterator is limited to 32 dimensions; default flattening accepts supported arrays up to 64. Legacy bitorder parsing is reproduced: pack accepts big/little prefixes, unpack first b/l; embedded NUL and unknown Lua option keys are rejected.

Empty-axis unpacking with positive output count deliberately produces defined zeros instead of the pinned NumPy2.5.3 uninitialized output. Another 358 source states are excluded from parity, separately documented and tested under the native zero-fill contract.

Bit packing uses scalar native loops; equivalent SIMD performance, typed scalar axis/count, foreign/index/subclass protocols, Python scalar classes, exact warning/exception hierarchy, huge allocations, every ABI and every input combination remain uncertified.

NumPy2.5.4 is the primary reference, not a claim that every2.5.4 change is implemented. Object arrays, StringDType, masked arrays, Python warning/exception protocols, MSVC and all ABIs remain uncertified.

Quantiles currently support six methods, nonempty scalar/vector fractions, real numeric input, axis/keepdims/out; weights, overwrite_input and complete signatures remain unavailable. Typed longdouble fractions pass through double parameters even when output dtype remains longdouble.
new_check_count_scope: Three new focused corpora only; legacy2700-case assertion count not included.
new_check_semantics: Empty retained axes and empty axis selections; dtype/promotion, shape, strides, flags, ownership and significant bytes. Median K-order layout and retained keepdims views. Nonfinite SVD/lstsq guards and condition numbers, exact accumulate output-shape validation including empty temporal dtype resolution. Inputs/output backing states after rejection. Scalar keepdims and extreme empty-view strides exercised through Lua and native API.

new_reference_tolerances.NaNs: scalar and array results compare classification; payload/sign not certified
new_reference_tolerances.longdouble: all ten significant x87 bytes checked; six padding bytes omitted

new_reference_language_adaptations.axes: Nonnegative NumPy axes become one-based Lua positions; negative axes retain meaning.
